1	"""grokking_optimizers.megakernel — Stage 6 feasibility solver + generator.
2	
3	Composes the per-arch kernel primitives into one fused **L3 persistent
4	megakernel per (model × optimizer × arch)** — 3 models × 11 optimizers × 3
5	archs = 99 pipelines (§1.5 L3, §1.6 all-99, §1.8 all-three-models).
6	
7	This module is the **automatic feasibility solver** (§1.9/§1.10): it reads each
8	component's register / shared-mem (LDS on AMD) budget from the ARCH_TABLE and
9	picks the highest fusion tier that fits per (model, optimizer, arch); it falls
10	back DOWN tiers when L3 doesn't fit, and **errors** (§1.11 — no silent slow
11	path) when even the lowest tier doesn't fit. The chosen plan is what the C++
12	generator (`csrc/fused/<arch>/`) emits, and what `fused_step` in dispatch.cpp
13	prefers when a fused TU is present (§1.12).
14	
15	Hardware-deferred: the *measured* register counts come from `ptxas
16	-v`/`rocm-llvm` on real silicon; here the solver uses calibrated per-component
17	estimates (recorded in HARDWARE_VALIDATION.md), so the tier selection is
18	🟡 until the on-device register report confirms it.
19	
20	🟡 WORKSTREAM-1 CAVEAT (register-pressure reduction): the component costs below
21	were LOWERED to reflect behavior-preserving SMEM-staging / rematerialization /

148	class FusionPlan:
149	    model: str
150	    optimizer: str
151	    arch: str
152	    tier: FusionTier
153	    regs: int
154	    smem: int
155	    budget_regs: int
156	    budget_smem: int
157	    note: str = ""

159	    @property
160	    def fits(self) -> bool:
161	        return self.tier > FusionTier.L0_UNFUSED

164	# Hopper setmaxnreg producer-warp-group floor (kProducerRegsF in
165	# fused_megakernel.cuh). The producer WG that runs the light staging + the
166	# optimizer tail is bounded at this allocation; the heavy model stages run on
167	# the consumer WG. See _tier_cost for how the §3.4 split changes the L3 peak.
168	_PRODUCER_WG_REGS = 32
169	
170	
171	def _tier_cost(model: str, optimizer: str,
172	               tier: FusionTier) -> Tuple[int, int]:
173	    """Peak (regs, smem) for a given fusion tier.
174	
175	    WORKSTREAM 1 (#6): the L3 fused kernel now runs as TWO Hopper warp-groups
176	    (setmaxnreg split, fused_megakernel.cuh). The heavy model forward/backward
177	    stages run on the CONSUMER warp-group; the light producer staging + the
178	    optimizer tail run on the PRODUCER warp-group. The SM register *ceiling* a
179	    single warp-group must satisfy is therefore the MAX of the two warp-groups'
180	    footprints, NOT the old sum (max(fwd,bwd) + opt). We bound the consumer WG
181	    by max(fwd,bwd) and the producer WG by the optimizer tail (which subsumes
182	    the producer floor), and take the max. smem is the MAX tile resident at
183	    once (the staged adjoint / attention buffers are summed into the component
184	    smem figures). 🟡 these are MODEL estimates — ptxas register allocation
185	    differs; the per-cell maxrregcount sweep (compile.py knob #1) + on-silicon
186	    `ptxas -v` are the source of truth.
187	    """
188	    fwd = _MODEL_FWD[model]
189	    bwd = _MODEL_BWD[model]
190	    opt = _OPT_COST[optimizer]
191	    if tier == FusionTier.L3_FWD_BWD_OPT:
192	        consumer_wg = max(fwd.regs, bwd.regs)          # heavy model stages
193	        producer_wg = max(opt.regs, _PRODUCER_WG_REGS)  # tail + staging
194	        regs = max(consumer_wg, producer_wg)            # §3.4 split: max, not sum
195	        smem = max(fwd.smem, bwd.smem, opt.smem)
196	    elif tier == FusionTier.L2_BWD_OPT:
197	        regs = bwd.regs + opt.regs
198	        smem = max(bwd.smem, opt.smem)
199	    elif tier == FusionTier.L1_OPT_ONLY:
200	        regs = opt.regs
201	        smem = opt.smem
202	    else:
203	        regs, smem = 0, 0
204	    return regs, smem

206	
207	def solve(model: str, optimizer: str, arch: str) -> FusionPlan:
208	    """§1.9/§1.10 feasibility solver: pick the highest fusion tier that fits.
209	
210	    Falls DOWN tiers when L3 doesn't fit; raises (§1.11 — no silent slow path)
211	    when even L1 (optimizer-only fusion) doesn't fit the arch budget.
212	
213	    Accepts both short names ("mamba", "decoder", "vit") and canonical names
214	    ("mamba3", "transformer_decoder", "vit") via canonicalize_model().
215	    """
216	    model = canonicalize_model(model)
217	    if model not in _MODEL_FWD:
218	        raise KeyError(f"unknown model '{model}'")
219	    if optimizer not in _OPT_COST:
220	        raise KeyError(f"unknown optimizer '{optimizer}'")
221	
222	    b = _arch_budget(arch)
223	
224	    # Pallas/TPU: XLA owns allocation; the megakernel is a single fused program
225	    # and always "fits" at this granularity. Report L3.
226	    if b.is_pallas:
227	        return FusionPlan(model, optimizer, arch, FusionTier.L3_FWD_BWD_OPT,
228	                          regs=0, smem=0, budget_regs=0, budget_smem=0,
229	                          note="pallas/XLA: single fused program, allocator-managed")
230	
231	    for tier in (FusionTier.L3_FWD_BWD_OPT,
232	                 FusionTier.L2_BWD_OPT,
233	                 FusionTier.L1_OPT_ONLY):
234	        regs, smem = _tier_cost(model, optimizer, tier)
235	        if regs <= b.max_regs_per_thread and smem <= b.max_smem_per_block:
236	            note = ""
237	            if tier != FusionTier.L3_FWD_BWD_OPT:
238	                # Record exactly which higher tier(s) busted, and on which
239	                # resource, so the coverage table is self-explaining.
240	                reasons = []
241	                for hi in (FusionTier.L3_FWD_BWD_OPT, FusionTier.L2_BWD_OPT):
242	                    if hi <= tier:
243	                        continue
244	                    hr, hs = _tier_cost(model, optimizer, hi)
245	                    over = []
246	                    if hr > b.max_regs_per_thread:
247	                        over.append(f"regs {hr}>{b.max_regs_per_thread}")
248	                    if hs > b.max_smem_per_block:
249	                        over.append(f"smem {hs}>{b.max_smem_per_block}")
250	                    if over:
251	                        reasons.append(f"{hi.name}({', '.join(over)})")
252	                note = f"fell back to {tier.name}; " + "; ".join(reasons)
253	            return FusionPlan(model, optimizer, arch, tier,
254	                              regs=regs, smem=smem,
255	                              budget_regs=b.max_regs_per_thread,
256	                              budget_smem=b.max_smem_per_block, note=note)
257	
258	    # §1.11: even L1 doesn't fit → hard error, never a silent slow path.
259	    regs, smem = _tier_cost(model, optimizer, FusionTier.L1_OPT_ONLY)
260	    raise RuntimeError(
261	        f"megakernel infeasible for ({model}, {optimizer}, {arch}): even "
262	        f"L1 optimizer-only fusion needs regs={regs}/smem={smem} but the arch "
263	        f"budget is regs={b.max_regs_per_thread}/smem={b.max_smem_per_block}. "
264	        f"No silent slow path (§1.11) — use the unfused per-op dispatch.")
265	
266	
267	def solve_all() -> List[FusionPlan]:
268	    """Solve the full 99-pipeline matrix. Infeasible cells are recorded with an
269	    L0 plan + the reason (so the table is complete) rather than raising, so the
270	    caller can see coverage at a glance."""
271	    plans: List[FusionPlan] = []
272	    for arch in MEGAKERNEL_ARCHS:
273	        for model in MODELS:
274	            for opt in OPTIMIZERS:
275	                try:
276	                    plans.append(solve(model, opt, arch))
277	                except RuntimeError as e:
278	                    b = _arch_budget(arch)
279	                    regs, smem = _tier_cost(model, opt, FusionTier.L1_OPT_ONLY)
280	                    plans.append(FusionPlan(
281	                        model, opt, arch, FusionTier.L0_UNFUSED,
282	                        regs=regs, smem=smem,
283	                        budget_regs=b.max_regs_per_thread,
284	                        budget_smem=b.max_smem_per_block,
285	                        note=f"INFEASIBLE: {e}"))
286	    return plans
287	
288	
289	def coverage_summary() -> Dict[str, int]:
290	    """Tier coverage across all 99 pipelines (for the consolidation report)."""
291	    plans = solve_all()
292	    out: Dict[str, int] = {t.name: 0 for t in FusionTier}
293	    for p in plans:
294	        out[p.tier.name] += 1
295	    return out

57	//  §1.3  SM-pinning: read the streaming-multiprocessor id via %smid.
58	//
59	//  The host launches exactly gridDim.x == #SMs CTAs (one persistent CTA per
60	//  SM) and uses sm_id() inside the kernel to index that SM's resident slice
61	//  of optimizer state, so the slice stays warm in this SM's L2 partition for
62	//  the whole step. On pre-sm_90 the asm is still valid (%smid exists since
63	//  sm_20); the guard only exists to keep a host-compile of this header clean.
64	// =========================================================================
65	__device__ __forceinline__ unsigned sm_id() {
66	#if defined(__CUDA_ARCH__)
67	    unsigned id;
68	    asm volatile("mov.u32 %0, %%smid;" : "=r"(id));
69	    return id;
70	#else
71	    return 0u;
72	#endif
73	}

75	// =========================================================================
76	//  §1.1 / §1.2  TaskQueue — global work counter + work-stealing.
77	//
78	//  One int in global memory (`g_next_task`, zero-initialized by the host).
79	//  Every CTA runs:
80	//      for (int t = q.next(); t < n_tasks; t = q.next()) process(t);
81	//  next() does `atomicAdd(g_next_task, 1)` — a CTA that drains its tensor
82	//  early just grabs the next index, so faster SMs steal work from the queue
83	//  with no static load-balancing (§1.2). The atomic is the ONLY synchronizer;
84	//  task bodies are independent (one parameter tensor each), so no fence is
85	//  needed on the *pull* — the fence belongs at the grid barrier between the
86	//  forward / backward / optimizer phases (§1.4), not on the per-task pull.
87	//
88	//  By convention ONE thread per CTA (the elected leader) pulls a task and
89	//  broadcasts it to the block via shared memory; `next_block()` packages that.
90	// =========================================================================
91	struct TaskQueue {
92	    int* g_next_task;   // global counter (host memset to 0 before launch)
93	    int  n_tasks;       // total parameter tensors to process this phase
94	
95	    __device__ __forceinline__ explicit TaskQueue(int* counter, int total)
96	        : g_next_task(counter), n_tasks(total) {}
97	
98	    // Per-thread atomic pull (used when every thread independently claims work,
99	    // e.g. a warp-granular schedule). Returns a task index that may be >=
100	    // n_tasks (caller bounds-checks).
101	    __device__ __forceinline__ int next() {
102	        return atomicAdd(g_next_task, 1);
103	    }
104	
105	    // Per-CTA pull: the leader thread does the single atomicAdd and broadcasts
106	    // the claimed index to the whole block through `smem_slot`. All threads in
107	    // the block then cooperate on that one tensor. Returns the claimed index.
108	    __device__ __forceinline__ int next_block(int* smem_slot) {
109	        if (threadIdx.x == 0) {
110	            *smem_slot = atomicAdd(g_next_task, 1);
111	        }
112	        __syncthreads();
113	        int t = *smem_slot;
114	        __syncthreads();   // ensure every thread read before slot is reused
115	        return t;
116	    }
117	};

119	// =========================================================================
120	//  §1.4  GridBarrier — hand-built, reusable, sense-reversing grid barrier.
121	//
122	//  State (all in global memory, host-zero-initialized):
123	//    arrived    — count of CTAs that have reached the current barrier
124	//    generation — flips/advances each time the barrier is crossed (the "sense"
125	//                 a late CTA waits on so an early CTA can't lap it)
126	//
127	//  The classic correctness hazard with a counter barrier is *reuse*: if you
128	//  just reset `arrived` to 0, a fast CTA can enter the NEXT barrier and
129	//  increment the counter before a slow CTA has observed the release of the
130	//  PREVIOUS one. The sense-reversing generation fixes this: each CTA samples
131	//  the generation on entry, then waits until the generation has ADVANCED
132	//  (the last arriver advances it), never touching `arrived` for reset on the
133	//  consumer side. The last CTA to arrive resets `arrived` to 0 and bumps the
134	//  generation in one release; everyone else spins on the generation.
135	//
136	//  Fences (§1.14):
137	//    * The releasing writes a CTA makes BEFORE the barrier (its phase output)
138	//      must be visible to peers AFTER the barrier. We publish arrival with a
139	//      __threadfence() (device-scope release) before the atomicAdd, and the
140	//      waiters do an acquire by reading the generation with volatile semantics
141	//      and a __threadfence() after the wait completes. Exactly two fences per
142	//      CTA per barrier — the minimum for a correct release/acquire pair.
143	//
144	//  Only thread 0 of each CTA participates in the cross-CTA handshake; the rest
145	//  of the block is gated by a __syncthreads() so the whole CTA leaves together.
146	// =========================================================================
147	struct GridBarrier {
148	    unsigned* g_arrived;      // CTAs arrived at current phase
149	    unsigned* g_generation;   // sense-reversing generation counter
150	    unsigned  n_ctas;         // gridDim.x (CTAs that must arrive)
151	
152	    __device__ __forceinline__ GridBarrier(unsigned* arrived,
153	                                            unsigned* generation,
154	                                            unsigned grid_ctas)
155	        : g_arrived(arrived), g_generation(generation), n_ctas(grid_ctas) {}
156	
157	    __device__ __forceinline__ void sync() const {
158	        // The block must fully reach the barrier before its leader publishes.
159	        __syncthreads();
160	
161	        if (threadIdx.x == 0) {
162	            // Sample the sense we are waiting to leave.
163	            unsigned my_gen =
164	                *reinterpret_cast<volatile unsigned*>(g_generation);
165	
166	            // §1.14 RELEASE: make this CTA's phase writes visible device-wide
167	            // BEFORE we announce arrival, so a peer that observes our arrival
168	            // (and crosses) also observes our outputs.
169	            __threadfence();
170	
171	            // Atomically join the arrival count. The CTA whose add completes
172	            // the set (== n_ctas) is the "last arriver".
173	            unsigned prev = atomicAdd(g_arrived, 1u);
174	            if (prev + 1u == n_ctas) {
175	                // Last arriver: clear the count for the NEXT phase, then bump
176	                // the generation. Order matters — reset arrived to 0 first,
177	                // then a release-store of the advanced generation so a CTA that
178	                // sees the new generation also sees arrived==0 when it next

564	# and tests/hw/decoder_oracle.py::decoder_param_layout() builds the same table

566	# parity test). Keep the shape constants here == decoder_oracle.py.

568	_DEC_DFF = 4 * _DEC_D

570	# ── HILL-CLIMB BENCH VARIANT (d-scaled decoder) ──────────────────────────────
571	# The persistent megakernel's compute roofline is diagnosed/optimized at a LARGE
572	# model width. _DEC_BENCH_D is the width the d-scaled BENCHMARK build compiles at;
573	# it does NOT touch the production d=128 path. decoder_layout_header() emits BOTH
574	# layouts into ONE header, selected by the compile flag SG_DEC_BENCH_LAYOUT (set
575	# ONLY by the bench TU / the _ops_bench variant; UNSET → the production d=128
576	# constants, byte-identical default). So the committed header carries both, the
577	# production _ops always sees d=128, and the variant build flips ONE flag. The

582	def _decoder_param_sizes(d: int = _DEC_D) -> List[int]:
583	    """Per-tensor numel in named_parameters() order (mirror of decoder_oracle.py
584	    decoder_param_spec()). 30 tensors; at d=128 total 422755. `d` is parametric
585	    so the d-scaled bench layout (SG_DEC_BENCH_LAYOUT) reuses the SAME shape
586	    formula — the per-tensor shapes are all functions of (d, dff=4d, vocab, seq),
587	    so a single d controls the whole table."""
588	    dff, v, seq = 4 * d, _DEC_VOCAB, _DEC_SEQ
589	    sizes = [v * d, seq * d]                      # tok, pos
590	    for _ in range(_DEC_LAYERS):
591	        sizes += [
592	            3 * d * d, 3 * d,                     # attn.in_proj_weight/bias
593	            d * d, d,                             # attn.out_proj.weight/bias
594	            d, d, d, d,                           # n1.w/b, n2.w/b
595	            dff * d, dff,                         # ff.0.weight/bias
596	            d * dff, d,                           # ff.2.weight/bias
597	        ]
598	    sizes += [d, d, v * d, v]                     # norm.w/b, out.weight/bias
599	    return sizes

606	    names (kDecOffsets/kDecSizes/dec_layout_check) across both is safe."""
607	    sizes = _decoder_param_sizes(d)
608	    offsets, acc = [], 0
609	    for n in sizes:
610	        offsets.append(acc)
611	        acc += n

618	        for i in range(0, len(arr), 10):

47	    int*     g_next = nullptr;        // int [1]
48	    unsigned* g_arrived = nullptr;    // unsigned [1]
49	    unsigned* g_generation = nullptr; // unsigned [1]
50	    float*   workspace = nullptr;     // float [dec_tc_workspace_floats(T,B,nCTA)]

55	DecTcLauncherScratch& dec_tc_launcher_scratch(int dev, int64_t need_floats) {
56	    static DecTcLauncherScratch s;
57	    if (s.dev != dev) {
58	        // First use on this device (or a device switch — the race is single-GPU,
59	        // but be honest if it ever moves): (re)allocate the counters.
60	        s.dev = dev;
61	        if (!s.g_next)      cudaMalloc(&s.g_next, sizeof(int));
62	        if (!s.g_arrived)   cudaMalloc(&s.g_arrived, sizeof(unsigned));
63	        if (!s.g_generation)cudaMalloc(&s.g_generation, sizeof(unsigned));

74	// mega_decoder_real_adamw_tc — the WIRED TC launcher. Boundary mirrors the scalar
75	// mega_decoder_real_adamw (dispatch.cpp extern-decls it with the same mirror
76	// types) EXCEPT it takes NO workspace pointer: the TC workspace is a different
77	// size from the scalar nCTA*total partials, so this TU allocates+owns it. `loss_out`
78	// still points into the caller's state[3*total] slot (dispatch reads it back).
79	//
80	// OPTID-GENERIC (owner baseline directive — all 33 cells on L3-TC): the fwd+bwd+
81	// grad-reduction is OPTIMIZER-INDEPENDENT (the same validated wgmma decoder kernel);
82	// ONLY the per-element optimizer TAIL (apply_optimizer<Opt>) differs, and that tail
83	// is the 14/0-apply-parity math already in opt_components.cuh. So this launcher
84	// takes `opt_id` (the OptId int) and dispatches to the matching kernel instantiation
85	// over the SAME state buffer. The state layout is [m | v | extra] (3*total) + loss:
86	//   * lion              uses m only (v/extra unread; bound harmlessly)
87	//   * adamw             uses m, v
88	//   * grokfast/grokadamw use m, v, ema  (ema == the `extra` slice, state + 2*total)
89	//   * neuralgrok        uses m, v, AND a psi-net weight pack the cell supplies in the
90	//                       `extra` slice (kPsiPackFloats floats); st.psi_W1/b1/W2 bind
91	//                       to those offsets, exactly as opt_components.cuh documents.
92	// The STAGED optimizers prodigy (P2.6 global-d) and muon (P2.7 grid-cooperative NS)
93	// ARE routed here: their precompute is an IN-KERNEL phase, so they remain a SINGLE
94	// persistent launch (the cases below). The SAM-coupled SG11/SG15/looksam and SG2 are
95	// NOT — they need a 2nd in-kernel fwd+bwd / a sharpness ABI field / a segmented sort
96	// that this single-launch path does not carry; dispatch.cpp gates them out (and
97	// wiring_check fails them loud with the cited reason). NeuralGrok is wired but its
98	// host-trained amplifier is a separate concern (the race fn gates it).
99	//
100	// ncta_cap: forwarded to the TC launcher (0 = one CTA/SM = full saturation, the
101	// shipped config). The race always passes 0.
102	cudaError_t mega_decoder_real_adamw_tc(
103	        PersistentContext ctx, float* params,
104	        const int* tokens, const int* targets, int B,
105	        float* state, float* grad, float* /*workspace_unused*/, float* loss_out,
106	        const int* sizes, const int* offsets,
107	        float lr, int step, const FusedScalars& scalars, cudaStream_t stream,
108	        int ncta_cap, int opt_id) {
109	    (void)sizes; (void)offsets;  // TC kernel reads kDecSizes/kDecOffsets directly.
110	
111	    const int64_t total = kDecTotalElems;
112	    const int T = B * dec::kSeq;
113	
114	    int dev = 0;
115	    cudaError_t err = cudaGetDevice(&dev);
116	    if (err != cudaSuccess) return err;
117	    int n_sms = 1;
118	    err = cudaDeviceGetAttribute(&n_sms, cudaDevAttrMultiProcessorCount, dev);
119	    if (err != cudaSuccess) return err;
120	    int nCTA = n_sms;
121	    if (ncta_cap > 0 && ncta_cap < nCTA) nCTA = ncta_cap;
122	
123	    const int64_t need = dec_tc_workspace_floats(T, B, nCTA);
124	    DecTcLauncherScratch& sc = dec_tc_launcher_scratch(dev, need);
125	
126	    // Re-point the ctx counters at THIS TU's cached counters (dispatch.cpp built
127	    // ctx pointing at its scalar DecoderScratch counters; the TC launcher zeroes
128	    // them per-launch, but they must be the ones this scratch owns so the grid
129	    // barrier is consistent with the workspace).
130	    ctx.g_next_task   = sc.g_next;
131	    ctx.g_arrived     = sc.g_arrived;
132	    ctx.g_generation  = sc.g_generation;
133	    ctx.n_tasks       = kDecNumTensors;  // parameter tensors for reduce+opt phases
134	
135	    // Bind the optimizer state slices. [m | v | extra] over the SAME state buffer;
136	    // each tail reads only its own buffers (opt_components.cuh guarantees unused
137	    // pointers are never dereferenced). ema/psi-net live in the `extra` slice.
138	    float* const m_slice     = state;
139	    float* const v_slice     = state + total;
140	    float* const extra_slice = state + 2 * total;
141	    FusedOptState st;
142	    st.exp_avg    = m_slice;
143	    st.exp_avg_sq = v_slice;
144	    st.ema        = extra_slice;          // grokfast/grokadamw slow-grad EMA
145	    // NeuralGrok psi-net pack (kPsiPackFloats floats at the head of `extra`): the
146	    // cell places [psi_W1 | psi_b1 | psi_W2 | psi_b2] there; bind the device pointers
147	    // so the apply reads real weights (psi_b2 is read on-device from psi_W2[kPsiHidden]).
148	    st.psi_W1     = extra_slice + kPsiW1Off;
149	    st.psi_b1     = extra_slice + kPsiB1Off;
150	    st.psi_W2     = extra_slice + kPsiW2Off;
151	    // PRODIGY (STAGED global-d) state bindings. The cell extends the state buffer
152	    // to [m | v | extra/s_track | loss | param_init | r_ema | s_ema | d_lr] (host
153	    // sizes it to >= 4*total + 4; see dispatch.fused_train_step). The `extra` slice
154	    // doubles as Prodigy's `s` trajectory accumulator (the apply reads st.s_track,
155	    // not st.ema — they alias here, harmless: Prodigy has no slow-grad EMA). The
156	    // trajectory anchor p0 (param_init) follows the loss slot; the 3 persisted
157	    // estimator scalars [r_ema | s_ema | d_lr] follow param_init. loss_out points at
158	    // state+3*total (dispatch's loss_slot), so param_init = loss_out + 1.
159	    st.s_track        = extra_slice;            // Prodigy `s` (per-element accumulator)
160	    st.param_init     = loss_out + 1;           // state + 3*total + 1
161	    st.prodigy_persist = loss_out + 1 + total;  // [r_ema | s_ema | d_lr]
162	    // LookSAM (MODEL-COUPLED SAM 2nd backward): sam_dir is the PERSISTENT cached SAM
163	    // direction (g_sam − g), carried across steps in the `extra` slice (aliases the
164	    // grokfast EMA / Prodigy s_track slot — harmless: LookSAM has none of those). The
165	    // in-kernel P2.4 phase WRITES it on SAM steps; the apply tail READS it every step.
166	    st.sam_dir        = extra_slice;            // [total] cached SAM direction
167	    // SuperGrok11/15 (MODEL-COUPLED SAM 2nd backward + per-tensor meta-net mu). State
168	    // layout: [m | v | mu | loss | sharpness(total) | phi_pack(4H+1)].
169	    //   * st.mu = the `extra` slice (recomputed each step by the P2.45 precompute; the
170	    //     apply reads it — it aliases sam_dir/ema/s_track, harmless: SG has none).
171	    //   * st.sharpness = loss_slot+1 (PERSISTED (g_sam−g)²; the P2.4 SAM 2nd backward
172	    //     writes it on SAM steps, the cached value is reused on intervening steps).
173	    //   * st.sg_phi_W1/b1/W2 = the phi pack at sharpness+total (host-scattered each step,
174	    //     like NeuralGrok's psi pack); sg_phi_b2 is read on-device from sg_phi_W2[H].
175	    st.mu             = extra_slice;            // [total] meta-net mu (P2.45-filled)
176	    {
177	        float* sharp_base = loss_out + 1;       // state + 3*total + 1
178	        float* phi_base   = sharp_base + total; // phi pack after sharpness
179	        st.sharpness = sharp_base;
180	        st.sg_phi_W1 = phi_base + kSgPhiW1Off;
181	        st.sg_phi_b1 = phi_base + kSgPhiB1Off;
182	        st.sg_phi_W2 = phi_base + kSgPhiW2Off;  // sg_phi_b2 read on-device from [H]
183	    }
184	    apply_scalars(st, scalars);   // FULL scalar set (un-frozen bc1/bc2/... + d0/d_coef/beta3 + rho/looksam_sam/sg_rescale)
185	    st.lr = lr;
186	
187	    DecoderTokenCtx tok;
188	    tok.tokens    = tokens;
189	    tok.targets   = targets;
190	    tok.B         = B;
191	    tok.workspace = sc.workspace;
192	    tok.loss_out  = loss_out;
193	
194	    // Dispatch to the matching kernel instantiation. The fwd+bwd is identical across
195	    // these OptIds; the template differs ONLY in the P3 apply_optimizer<Opt> tail.
196	    // Unsupported opt_ids return cudaErrorInvalidValue → dispatch.cpp throws LOUD (no
197	    // silent scalar/adamw fallback — the no-suppression rule). The STAGED/model-coupled
198	    // optimizers are intentionally NOT cases here (they cannot run as a single launch).
199	    switch (static_cast<OptId>(opt_id)) {
200	        case OptId::AdamW:
201	            return launch_fused_decoder_megakernel_tc<OptId::AdamW>(
202	                ctx, params, tok, grad, lr, step, st, stream, nCTA);
203	        case OptId::Lion:
204	            return launch_fused_decoder_megakernel_tc<OptId::Lion>(
205	                ctx, params, tok, grad, lr, step, st, stream, nCTA);
206	        case OptId::Grokfast:
207	            return launch_fused_decoder_megakernel_tc<OptId::Grokfast>(
208	                ctx, params, tok, grad, lr, step, st, stream, nCTA);
209	        case OptId::GrokAdamW:
210	            return launch_fused_decoder_megakernel_tc<OptId::GrokAdamW>(
211	                ctx, params, tok, grad, lr, step, st, stream, nCTA);
212	        case OptId::NeuralGrok:
213	            return launch_fused_decoder_megakernel_tc<OptId::NeuralGrok>(
214	                ctx, params, tok, grad, lr, step, st, stream, nCTA);
215	        case OptId::Prodigy:
216	            // STAGED global-d: the SAME single persistent launch — the d-estimate
217	            // cross-tensor reduction is an IN-KERNEL phase (P2.6, between B2 and P3),
218	            // not a separate launch. st carries param_init/prodigy_persist/d0/d_coef/
219	            // beta3; the kernel decays+accumulates the EMA, updates d, applies.
220	            return launch_fused_decoder_megakernel_tc<OptId::Prodigy>(
221	                ctx, params, tok, grad, lr, step, st, stream, nCTA);
222	        case OptId::Muon:
223	            // STAGED grid-cooperative Newton-Schulz (wave-2 decoder lane): the SAME
224	            // single persistent launch — the NS orthogonalization of the 11 2D weights
225	            // (tok/pos/in_proj/out_proj/ff.0/ff.2/out) is an IN-KERNEL phase (P2.7,
226	            // between B2/P2.6 and P3), grid-barrier-looped per matrix, NOT a separate
227	            // launch. The per-matrix NS scratch lives in the workspace (dec_tc_muon_floats,
228	            // carved after the Prodigy reduce slots). The persistent momentum buffer is
229	            // the m-slice (st.exp_avg); the 1D/non-2D weights take the AdamW tail in P3
230	            // reading the INDEPENDENT aux_lr/aux_betas (eager Muon adamw_* group). The
231	            // vit twin (mega_vit_real_adamw_tc_launcher.cu) proved this routing.
232	            return launch_fused_decoder_megakernel_tc<OptId::Muon>(
233	                ctx, params, tok, grad, lr, step, st, stream, nCTA);
234	        case OptId::LookSAM:
235	            // MODEL-COUPLED SAM 2nd backward (wave-2 decoder lane): the SAME single
236	            // persistent launch — the perturb→2nd in-kernel fwd+bwd→sam_dir=g_sam−g is
237	            // an IN-KERNEL phase (P2.4, between B2 and P2.5/P3), gated to every-k SAM
238	            // steps by st.looksam_sam. The transient backup + g_sam buffers live in the
239	            // workspace (dec_tc_looksam_floats, carved after the Muon scratch); sam_dir
240	            // persists in the extra slice (st.sam_dir, bound above). The apply tail (P3)
241	            // blends g_adj=(1−α)g+α·sam_dir and runs AdamW. NOT a separate launch.
242	            return launch_fused_decoder_megakernel_tc<OptId::LookSAM>(
243	                ctx, params, tok, grad, lr, step, st, stream, nCTA);
244	        case OptId::SuperGrok11:
245	            // MODEL-COUPLED SAM 2nd backward + per-tensor meta-net mu/gate (wave-3
246	            // decoder lane): the SAME single persistent launch. The SAM 2nd backward
247	            // (P2.4, sharpness=(g_sam−g)²) + the per-tensor mu precompute (P2.45,
248	            // mu=rescale·phi(g,sharpness)) + the per-tensor cosine gate are ALL
249	            // in-kernel phases between B2 and P3; the apply tail (sg11_sweep_b_step:
250	            // smart_grad=g+(1−gate)·alpha·mu, AdamW) runs in P3. The SAM scratch reuses
251	            // the looksam buffers (dec_tc_looksam_floats); sharpness + the phi pack ride
252	            // the extended state buffer (bound above). NOT a separate launch.
253	            return launch_fused_decoder_megakernel_tc<OptId::SuperGrok11>(
254	                ctx, params, tok, grad, lr, step, st, stream, nCTA);
255	        case OptId::SuperGrok15:
256	            // Same SAM 2nd backward + mu precompute as SG11, but SIMPLER tail: the gate
257	            // is a host scalar (st.gate = sigmoid(accuracy)), NO per-tensor cosine stage;
258	            // the apply tail (sg15_sweep_b_step) does the per-coord alpha clip + smart_grad
259	            // = g + gate·a·mu + AdamW. Single persistent launch.
260	            return launch_fused_decoder_megakernel_tc<OptId::SuperGrok15>(
261	                ctx, params, tok, grad, lr, step, st, stream, nCTA);
262	        default:
263	            return cudaErrorInvalidValue;  // STAGED/coupled opt not single-launch TC
264	    }

267	// mega_decoder_sg2_tc — the DEDICATED SuperGrok2 TC launcher. SG2 needs the FULL
268	// CSA/HCA/PEER/GRU meta-net weight bundle (26 HBM pointers, model-independent) +
269	// per-tensor scalar ARRAYS (alpha/gru_decay/lamb_eff/beta1/bc1/bc2, length P) +
270	// the meta-net state (m/v/mu/slow/gru_state/sharpness), none of which fit the
271	// FusedScalars POD or the generic mega_decoder_real_adamw_tc boundary. So this is
272	// a PARALLEL entry (the generic launcher + the 28 byte-identical cells are
273	// UNTOUCHED). It binds the SG2 state slices, threads the weight bundle + scalar
274	// arrays through FusedOptState's sg2_* fields, and dispatches the OptId::SuperGrok2
275	// kernel instantiation (its P3-SG2 phase runs sg2_meta_stages per tensor: STAGE -1
276	// in-kernel segmented sort → CSA/HCA/GRU/PEER/apply, reading st.sharpness from the
277	// SAM 2nd backward (P2.4, shared with SG11/15)).
278	//
279	// STATE LAYOUT (host sizes it; this carves it):
280	//   [m(total) | v(total) | mu(total) | loss(1) | sharpness(total) | slow(total)
281	//    | gru_state(total*GH)]   ⇒ min_state = (4+1+GH)*total + 1   (GH=gru_hidden=4)
282	// perm/unsort are built IN-KERNEL into the per-CTA workspace (NOT state).
283	cudaError_t mega_decoder_sg2_tc(
284	        PersistentContext ctx, float* params,
285	        const int* tokens, const int* targets, int B,
286	        float* state, float* grad, float* loss_out,
287	        // SG2 meta-net weight bundle (HBM, fp32, model-independent), in SG2Weights order.
288	        const float* input_proj_W, const float* input_proj_b,
289	        const float* csa_q_W, const float* csa_k_W, const float* csa_v_W, const float* csa_out_W,
290	        const float* csa_compress_w, const float* csa_idx_DQ, const float* csa_idx_K,
291	        const float* hca_q_W, const float* hca_k_W, const float* hca_v_W, const float* hca_out_W,
292	        const float* gru_Wz, const float* gru_bz, const float* gru_Wr, const float* gru_br,
293	        const float* gru_Wh, const float* gru_bh,
294	        const float* peer_query_Ws, const float* prod_keys_A, const float* prod_keys_B,
295	        const float* expert_W1, const float* expert_b1, const float* expert_W2, const float* expert_b2,
296	        // per-tensor scalar arrays (device, length kDecNumTensors).
297	        const float* sc_alpha, const float* sc_gru_decay, const float* sc_lamb_eff,
298	        const float* sc_beta1, const float* sc_bc1, const float* sc_bc2,
299	        // shared scalars + the SAM 2nd-backward gate (SG2 reuses the LookSAM P2.4
300	        // machinery: rho = perturbation radius, sam_on = every-k SAM-step gate).
301	        float rescale, float beta2, float lr, float wd, float eps,
302	        float rho, float sam_on,
303	        int step, cudaStream_t stream, int ncta_cap) {
304	    const int64_t total = kDecTotalElems;
305	    // gru_state spans total*GH (GH=DecSG2Dims::gru_hidden); the layout is fixed by
306	    // the kernel's SG2State carve, so the slices below need no GH arithmetic here.
307	    const int T = B * dec::kSeq;
308	
309	    int dev = 0;
310	    cudaError_t err = cudaGetDevice(&dev);
311	    if (err != cudaSuccess) return err;
312	    int n_sms = 1;
313	    err = cudaDeviceGetAttribute(&n_sms, cudaDevAttrMultiProcessorCount, dev);
314	    if (err != cudaSuccess) return err;
315	    int nCTA = n_sms;
316	    if (ncta_cap > 0 && ncta_cap < nCTA) nCTA = ncta_cap;
317	
318	    const int64_t need = dec_tc_workspace_floats(T, B, nCTA);
319	    DecTcLauncherScratch& sc = dec_tc_launcher_scratch(dev, need);
320	    ctx.g_next_task   = sc.g_next;
321	    ctx.g_arrived     = sc.g_arrived;
322	    ctx.g_generation  = sc.g_generation;
323	    ctx.n_tasks       = kDecNumTensors;
324	
325	    // Bind the SG2 state slices: [m | v | mu | loss | sharpness | slow | gru_state].
326	    FusedOptState st;
327	    st.exp_avg     = state;                       // m
328	    st.exp_avg_sq  = state + total;               // v
329	    st.mu          = state + 2 * total;           // expert-output EMA
330	    // loss_out points at state + 3*total (dispatch's loss slot).
331	    float* sharp_base = loss_out + 1;             // state + 3*total + 1
332	    st.sharpness   = sharp_base;                  // (g_sam − g)² (SAM 2nd backward, P2.4)
333	    st.sg2_slow    = sharp_base + total;          // grokfast slow-grad EMA
334	    st.sg2_gru_state = st.sg2_slow + total;       // [total*GH] per-element GRU state
335	    // meta-net weight bundle (HBM).
336	    st.sg2_input_proj_W = input_proj_W; st.sg2_input_proj_b = input_proj_b;
337	    st.sg2_csa_q_W = csa_q_W; st.sg2_csa_k_W = csa_k_W; st.sg2_csa_v_W = csa_v_W;
338	    st.sg2_csa_out_W = csa_out_W; st.sg2_csa_compress_w = csa_compress_w;
339	    st.sg2_csa_idx_DQ = csa_idx_DQ; st.sg2_csa_idx_K = csa_idx_K;
340	    st.sg2_hca_q_W = hca_q_W; st.sg2_hca_k_W = hca_k_W; st.sg2_hca_v_W = hca_v_W;
341	    st.sg2_hca_out_W = hca_out_W;
342	    st.sg2_gru_Wz = gru_Wz; st.sg2_gru_bz = gru_bz; st.sg2_gru_Wr = gru_Wr;
343	    st.sg2_gru_br = gru_br; st.sg2_gru_Wh = gru_Wh; st.sg2_gru_bh = gru_bh;
344	    st.sg2_peer_query_Ws = peer_query_Ws; st.sg2_prod_keys_A = prod_keys_A;
345	    st.sg2_prod_keys_B = prod_keys_B;
346	    st.sg2_expert_W1 = expert_W1; st.sg2_expert_b1 = expert_b1;
347	    st.sg2_expert_W2 = expert_W2; st.sg2_expert_b2 = expert_b2;

"""grokking_optimizers.megakernel_engine — §8.4 fused-kernel ↔ framework adapter.

THE TRICKY PART (§8.4). DeepSpeed and Megatron-LM are both built around a
**separate** forward / backward / `optimizer.step()` interface:

    out  = engine(batch)        # forward
    engine.backward(loss)       # backward — populates .grad on every param
    engine.step()               # optimizer.step() + grad clear

But the Stage-6 megakernel (``grokking_optimizers.megakernel``) is a **fused L3
single launch**: one persistent kernel does forward **and** backward **and** the
optimizer update inside one kernel invocation (``FusionTier.L3_FWD_BWD_OPT``).
There is no separate backward to hook, and no separate `.step()` — the fused
launch already did all three. The framework's contract and the fused kernel's
contract are therefore in direct conflict.

This module is the **adapter** that reconciles them. It does two things:

1. :class:`MegakernelOptimizer` — a ``torch.optim.Optimizer`` subclass that
   presents the fused step as a standard ``.step()`` so DeepSpeed/Megatron can
   drive it as a ``client_optimizer``. Its ``.step()`` is where the actual fused
   launch is invoked (for L3) or where the inner optimizer's real ``.step()``
   runs (for L1/L2). It degrades to a plain pass-through optimizer when no
   framework is present.

2. :class:`FusedBackwardHook` — intercepts / no-ops the framework's separate
   ``.backward()`` **when the fused path owns fwd+bwd+opt** (L3). When the fused
   kernel already produced gradients-and-update in the forward launch, letting
   the framework run its own autograd backward would (a) waste a full backward
   pass and (b) double-apply the update. The hook short-circuits the framework
   backward and instead just marks gradients as "owned by the fused kernel" so
   ``.step()`` knows not to re-run them.

## 2. PERSISTENT KERNEL STRUCTURE — phases, GridBarrier, %smid pinning

The real kernel (`fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh`) is a SINGLE persistent
`__global__` whose phases are separated by in-kernel grid barriers (NO
intermediate kernel launches). Two bodies:

### Scalar body `fused_decoder_megakernel<Opt>` (`:196`) — gated OFF for prod
- `#ifndef SG_DEC_SCALAR_MEGAKERNEL / #define …=1` (`:137` region), but dispatch
  never routes to it; the TC engine carries every wired cell (`:122-125`).
- Phase layout (`:18-37`, 5 phases / 4 grid barriers — header comment):
  - **P0** (`:216`): each CTA zeroes its own grad-partial slab + loss slot.
  - **B0** barrier (`bar.sync()`, `:219`).
  - **P1** (`:221`): batch-parallel fwd+bwd. Each CTA owns a fixed contiguous
    batch slice `[b0,b1)` by `blockIdx.x` (`:227-229`), processes samples one at
    a time CTA-cooperatively, accumulates per-CTA weight-grad partials (no
    atomics → deterministic), sums fp32 NLL.
  - **B1** barrier (`:243`).
  - **P2** (`:245`): deterministic cross-CTA reduce — work-steal param
    element-ranges, sum partials in ASCENDING CTA index (order fixed →
    deterministic regardless of which CTA grabs the task) (`:257-261`); loss
    reduced in fp64 by CTA 0 (`:267-271`).
  - **B2** barrier with FUSED task-counter reset: `bar.sync_reset(ctx.g_next_task)`
    (`:273`).
  - **P3** (`:275`): real optimizer tail `apply_optimizer<Opt>` over reduced grad,
    work-stealing the 30 param tensors (`:281-289`).
  - No barrier after P3 — kernel exits (`:37`).

### TC body `fused_decoder_megakernel_tc<Opt>` (`:673`) — the WIRED kernel
- Single `__global__`, `__launch_bounds__(SG_TC_MEGA_BLOCK)` where
  `SG_TC_MEGA_BLOCK = 256` (`:348`).
- Same P0→B0→P1→B1→P2→B2→P3 skeleton, plus extra in-kernel phases folded in for
  STAGED/coupled optimizers WITHOUT extra launches:
  - Prodigy global-d reduction: P2.6 between B2 and P3
    (`mega_decoder_real_adamw_tc_launcher.cu:216-221`).
  - Muon grid-cooperative Newton-Schulz: P2.7 (`launcher.cu:222-233`).
  - LookSAM / SG11 / SG15 / SG2 SAM 2nd backward: P2.4 (a 2nd in-kernel fwd+bwd)
    (`launcher.cu:234-261`; `fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh:694-698` flags
    `kSamCoupled`).
- Per-phase profiling via `clock64()` deltas in `g_dec_prof_max[8]`
  (`:660-669`): [0]=P1 fwd, [1]=P1 bwd, [2]=B1 wait, [3]=P2 dW-GEMM, [4]=P2
  grad-assembly, [5]=P3 tail, [6]=B2 wait, [7]=B0 wait.

### GridBarrier (`csrc/fused/megakernel_common.cuh:147-255`)
- Hand-built, reusable, sense-reversing: state = `g_arrived` (count) +
  `g_generation` (sense). Last arriver resets `arrived=0`, fences, bumps
  generation; others spin on generation (`:173-201`).
- NO cooperative launch needed → scales past the cooperative-grid CTA cap
  (`:28-29`).
- Exactly 2 fences per CTA per barrier (release before arrival publish, acquire
  after wait) (`:136-142`, `:169`, `:205`).
- `__nanosleep` exponential backoff (cap 1024) on the spin (`:193-199`).
- `sync_reset(reset_counter)` (`:222-254`) folds the task-counter reset into the
  last-arriver critical section → 4 grid barriers collapse to 2 per L3 step.
- Only thread 0 participates in the cross-CTA handshake; rest gated by
  `__syncthreads()` (`:158-159`, `:208-209`).

### %smid pinning (`megakernel_common.cuh:65-73`)
- `sm_id()` reads `%%smid` via inline asm. Host launches exactly `gridDim.x ==
  #SMs` CTAs (one persistent CTA per SM) so each SM's optimizer-state slice stays
  L2-warm (`:57-63`). nCTA = `cudaDevAttrMultiProcessorCount`
  (`fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh:1519-1521`).

### TaskQueue / work-stealing (`megakernel_common.cuh:91-117`)
- One global atomic counter `g_next_task`; `next()` = `atomicAdd(…,1)` IS the
  steal (no static partition) (`:101-103`). `next_block(smem_slot)` = leader pulls
  + broadcasts (`:108-116`).

### Single-launch confirmation
- The TC kernel is launched by a PLAIN `<<<grid, block, dyn_smem, stream>>>`
  (`fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh:1566`), NOT `cudaLaunchCooperativeKernel`. The
  grid barrier replaces cooperative launch. ViT
  (`fused_vit_megakernel.cuh:1178`) and Mamba (`fused_mamba_megakernel.cuh:1273`)
  use the identical `<<<grid, block, dyn_smem, stream>>>` pattern.

  occ ≥ 1 or returns `cudaErrorLaunchOutOfResources`
  (`fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh:1540-1545`). Counters memset to 0 per launch
  (`:1557-1559`). Requires `B % 16 == 0` (`:1555`).

**So: each WIRED real cell IS a single `__global__` launch** (one launch per
training step), with fwd→barrier→bwd-reduce→barrier→opt internal phases. The
33 generated surrogate cells are NOT independently compiled single launches —
they call a missing `launch_fused_megakernel` and never link.
